comments.text:
Whether you take this as yuri or not, its so unique that the narrative shows them unlearning idolising one another. Miku & Teto have a tint of each other's color in their eyes. Teto is initially looking up and walking up to Miku, but after 6 months, its Miku sat behind and leaning over to meet Teto. The team behind this video gives the world a painterly, watercolor texture, a beautiful story. But it's almost too good to be true? I really, really love how, when they float in the water, both of their hairstyles seem larger and more vibrant than in reality. And as a conclusion, they both choose to tie their pigtails lower when dancing, literally lowering their most iconic attributes to appear...mundane or approachable. This whole thing came about because of a dance class, an average thing that you might only do once a week. Do they even meet outside of this? Do they really know each other?

They both look disappointed because they realise they're the same. There's no fantasy. They're normal girls dancing in storage room dresses. Thats not to say this interpretation is a negative or tragic one, but rather, this feels like a neutral epiphany, waking up from an afternoon nap and realising you have work to do. If there was actually skill gap, if the other was truly unreachable, they wouldnt dance in unison like they do. In the final pose theres no blush colors, only them, and it halts in a blink - neither knows where to go from here. 

I spent awhile confused on how the title related to the story present here, and this is just a little take I made up regarding that.

Maybe they did only love each other from a distance, but it's better that they realised at all. This is still a healthy outcome.
